title: Read the pattern from its end
hook: Must a search look at every letter of the text?

knows: KMP never moves back in the text (kmp-never-steps-back)
doesNotKnow: that comparing the pattern from its end lets you skip text and look at fewer characters than the text has

misconception: Any search must look at every character of the text at least once.
objective: The learner can explain that a mismatch against a text letter that is not in the pattern rules out every placement covering it, so Horspool finds EXAMPLE in a 24-letter text with 15 comparisons in 5 placements and never reads 11 letters, while the plain method reads all 24 with 27 comparisons.

claims.text: Horspool finds EXAMPLE in "HERE IS A SIMPLE EXAMPLE" with 15 character comparisons in 5 placements.
claims.source: Builder's node script (2026-10-14, algo2-sc) and HORS in Demo.tsx: compare right to left; on a miss slide by the table entry of the text letter under the pattern's last position. Placements 0, 7, 9, 15, 17; slide log 0:S->7, 7:P->2, 9:E->6, 15:P->2, 17:match. A comparison is one text letter against one pattern letter. The brief said 4 alignments; the spec corrected it to 5 and this build reproduces 5. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own Horspool in node (scratchpad fc22/bm.mjs, written independently): 15 comparisons, 5 placements 0,7,9,15,17; slides 0:S->7, 7:P->2, 9:E->6, 15:P->2, 17:match. Matches HORS in Demo.tsx and the reveal (computed from HORS).

claims.text: The plain left-to-right method takes 27 comparisons over 18 placements and reads all 24 letters.
claims.source: Builder's node script and PLAIN in Demo.tsx: placements 0..17, each reading left to right until a miss or a full match; 27 comparisons; the set of text positions read has 24 members. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own naive search (scratchpad fc22/bm.mjs): 27 comparisons, 18 placements (0..17), 24 distinct text positions read; match at 17. Matches PLAIN in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: Horspool never reads 11 of the 24 letters.
claims.source: Builder's node script: the set of text positions Horspool compares has 13 members (position 13 is read twice), so 24 - 13 = 11 are never read. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own Horspool: 13 distinct text positions read, 24 - 13 = 11 never read. Reveal and lane readout compute T.length - read.size.

claims.text: The slide table for EXAMPLE is E 6, X 5, A 4, M 3, P 2, L 1, any other letter 7.
claims.source: Horspool's table: for each letter in the pattern except the last position, the distance from its last occurrence to the end (E at 0 -> 6, X 5, A 4, M 3, P 2, L 1); letters not in P[0..5] get the pattern length 7. Horspool 1980, Software: Practice and Experience 10(6) (from memory, not opened). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Derivation re-done: shift(c) = m-1-(last index of c in P[0..5]); E (index 0; the E at 6 is excluded) 6, X 5, A 4, M 3, P 2, L 1, absent 7. Own node table matches SHIFT/TABLE in Demo.tsx and the stage's Slide row.

claims.text: The first check met S; S is not in EXAMPLE, so no placement covering it could match, and the pattern jumped 7.
claims.source: At placement 0 the pattern's last letter E is under text position 6, which is S. Every placement 1..6 would put some pattern letter over that S, and S is not in EXAMPLE, so none can match; the next possible placement is 7. Node log confirms the first slide is 7. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): At placement 0 text[6] = S (pattern end), S not in EXAMPLE; placements 1..6 all put a pattern letter over position 6, so none can match; own run's first slide is 7. Reveal sentence computed from HORS[0].

claims.text: Horspool compares from the pattern's end and, on a miss, slides by the table entry of the text letter under the pattern's end.
claims.source: Horspool 1980, 'Practical fast searching in strings', Software: Practice and Experience; a simplification of Boyer and Moore 1977, 'A fast string searching algorithm', Commun. ACM 20(10). CLRS 4e ch. 32 (chapter only). Citations from memory; check before publishing. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): The sentence describes the stage's algorithm, which I traced (c1). Attribution: Horspool, Software: Practice and Experience 10(6):501-506 (1980) confirmed as bibliographic data by web-search snippets (Wikipedia, NIST DADS listings); the paper PDF host was blocked (proxy 403), so the paper itself was NOT opened. Boyer-Moore 1977 CACM 20(10) and CLRS ch. 32 not opened (from memory).

claims.text: The text "HERE IS A SIMPLE EXAMPLE" has 24 characters, counting spaces.
claims.source: Count: T.length = 24 in Demo.tsx. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own count: "HERE IS A SIMPLE EXAMPLE".length = 24 (node).

claims.text: At placement 9 Horspool matched 4 letters (E, L, P, M), then missed on I; it slid 6, by the table entry for the E under the pattern's end, not 7. The stage log reads "Horspool slides: S 7 · P 2 · E 6 (miss on I) · P 2 · found".
claims.source: HORS in Demo.tsx (v2) and the builder's trace: placement 9 puts the pattern over text[9..15] = " SIMPLE"; text[15]=E matches E, L, P, M match, text[11]=I vs pattern A misses; the key is text[15]=E, SHIFT[E]=6, next placement 15. The reveal sentence and the log are computed from HORS (EPARTIAL, slideLabel). Builder algo2-sc, 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own Horspool run: offsets 0 (S, slide 7), 7 (P, 2), 9 (E L P M matched, miss on I, slide 6 by E), 15 (P, 2), found at 17; 15 comparisons. slideLabel log: 'Horspool slides: S 7 · P 2 · E 6 (miss on I) · P 2 · found'. 'Placement 9' is the 0-based text offset of the third placement (not shown on stage).

recall.question: Searching right to left from a pattern's end, you meet a text letter that does not occur in the pattern at all. What can you do?
options: Slide the pattern past that letter entirely
Go back and re-read the text from the start
recall.why: No placement that covers a letter missing from the pattern can match, so the whole pattern jumps past it and those letters are never read.
